extracted.intended_audience: regulated businesses, industry trade associations, commenters, economists, and lawyers engaged with the FTC's Negative Option Rule rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the substantive compliance, evidentiary, and analytic criteria the FTC used in its Negative Option Rule final Statement of Basis and Purpose, including disclosure and cancellation requirements, methodologies for cost estimation, PRA scope, and how enforcement/counting decisions were treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements of the final Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule requires disclosure of: the fact consumers will be charged; the amount(s) they will be charged; when the consumer must act (by deadline or frequency) to prevent or stop charges; and the information needed for the consumer to find the simple cancellation mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple cancellation mechanism requirement (ROSCA/finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation mechanisms must be 'simple' under ROSCA and the final Rule; online cancellation includes cancellation by email or within the marketer's app; where online cancellation was not offered historically, the Commission treats instances as telephonic cancellations for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances requiring mailed-in returns likely would not satisfy ROSCA's 'simple' requirement; when sellers failed to disclose cancellation methods, the Commission assumed telephonic cancellation could take place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry between enrollment and cancellation mechanisms / extra mechanism for in-person enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation mechanisms should be at least as easy to use as the enrollment mechanism; the final Rule requires offering an extra cancellation mechanism for in-person enrollments (which can be met through existing telephonic capabilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For firms that enroll customers by telephone, online, and in person, existing telephonic customer service may satisfy the extra mechanism requirement for in-person enrollments; the Commission required online cancellation only for the portion of consumers who enroll online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic assumption on churn rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission assumes average, aggregate, monthly voluntary churn rates are additive across months and does not assume a 3% per month 'decay' in the number of subscribers; consumers may cancel and later re-enroll, so churn cancels can be additive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission did not adjust reported churn rates to account for survey findings (e.g., that some consumers never cancel) because such loyalty is already reflected in the denominator of reported churn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality/specificity requirement for commenter cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters submitting cost estimates must provide itemized, disaggregated, and specific estimates tied to the particular features of the final Rule; aggregated, non-specific, or idiosyncratic compliance cost claims are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of insufficiency: NCTA's $12–$25 million estimate lacked itemization; IFA provided aggregated hours without labor input types; Carrigan-Walster's estimates replicated NPRM assumptions without tailoring to the final Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for estimating number of affected firms (NAICS usage and adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff used U.S. Census NAICS data to identify industries where sellers may offer negative option features (initially ~530,000 firms) and estimated that only a fraction (approx. 20%, ~106,000 entities) offer negative option features; where NAICS data were unavailable, staff used its own estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The estimate excludes entities possibly outside FTC authority; no commenter proposed a better alternative firm count, though some challenged the inclusion of certain B2B providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of labor wage proxies and time assumptions in cost valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission values labor inputs using BLS mean hourly wages (examples: lawyers $84.84; web developers $51.90; sales $25.62; clerical $20.94), averages where appropriate, and assumes a range of one to ten hours for minor website modifications or compliance checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using web developer time as a proxy for the worker time to create online offers or to implement small website changes is consistent with prior NPRM approaches but must be applied only when appropriate to the final Rule's regulatory baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption that hosting platforms and subscription-management tools reduce incremental costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where marketers use hosting platforms or payment processors (e.g., Shopify) or subscription-management services (e.g., Chargebee), the Commission assumes the incremental cost of using those tools to provide account management and cancellation functionality is zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shopify and similar services provide subscription management and cancellation tools as part of their offerings; fees to merchants vary, but the incremental cost of enabling such management is treated as negligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA scope and exemption for usual business records
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA analysis focuses strictly on information collection requirements created or affected by the amendments; under 5 CFR 1320.3(b)(2), time, effort, and resources spent on compiling and maintaining business records that are usual and customary do not constitute an Information Collection Request burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of cross-pled and pre-ROSCA matters in enforcement tallies
rubrics_metrics.description: In tallying enforcement matters the Commission includes matters where ROSCA and TSR counts were cross-pled as section 5 counts; matters resolved before ROSCA that addressed online marketing conduct are treated as ROSCA matters for assessing incremental benefits; when cancellation methods were multiple (e.g., online and telephonic), staff sometimes attributed half to telephonic and half to online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment simplifies analysis where records are incomplete; in a few matters no cancellation method was disclosed, and where necessary the Commission assumed telephonic cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of transferring assumptions from unrelated rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission rejects cost inputs and assumptions copied from other rulemakings (e.g., Unfair or Deceptive Fees NPRM) when those inputs are not incremental to compliance with the final Rule or are inappropriate given differing regulatory baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Carrigan-Walster adopted units of specialized labor from a different NPRM that the Commission found not representative of incremental compliance costs here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of anecdotes and non-representative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdotes or data about 'top' or 'largest' companies, or general statements without representative sampling or disaggregation, are not sufficiently reliable evidence for the Commission's cost-benefit analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NCTA anecdotes on enrollment channels and complaint rates and IHRSA statements about 'many' fitness clubs lacked the detail necessary for staff estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign impact assessments as informative analogs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may look to foreign impact assessments (e.g., U.K. Impact Assessment, Ofcom) to inform analogous burdens such as familiarization costs, recognizing differences in regimes but treating some costs (like reading and understanding rules) as comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ofcom, after stakeholder consultation, estimated ongoing notification costs by focusing on letters as the medium with significant ongoing costs—an approach the Commission referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope sensitivity regarding telemarketers and small subpopulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because certain subpopulations (e.g., telemarketing firms) constitute a small share of all firms covered, excluding or treating them differently in analysis is not expected to materially bias aggregate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of some contracts as non-negative-option (installment vs negative option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly contracts that do not auto-renew but apportion payments over 12 months are installment plans and not negative option plans; other firms may operate on pay-as-you-go bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data gaps and limits on subscriber-sample representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's sample for subscriber counts included firms for which U.S. subscriber data were available but omitted some firms for which only global or no subscriber data could be located, limiting representativeness of sampled subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Commission found U.S. subscriber estimates for Amazon, Ancestry, Hulu, Netflix, Paramount+, Boston Globe, NYT, but not for others like Savage Fenty, Daily Harvest, Deliveroo; some firms reported only global subscriber data.
